method: coverage-driven: enumerated every section of price_service.py (28 sections) + 20 sibling services + all 53 ENABLE_* flags with defaults, then walked each. Every finding reproduced by executing the real functions in this tree (zero network).

findings.title: WooCommerce branch never relabels a CONVERTED price — a foreign price banks as a genuine Bahrain shelf price (7d TTL + genuine-share KPI + race-confirming)
findings.claim: `_extract_woocommerce_price` converts a foreign price to BHD but leaves `source_method` at `page_scrape` — the only structured branch that omits the `converted_usd` relabel every sibling performs.
findings.evidence: price_service.py:13109 stamps `source_method: "page_scrape"`; :13119-13130 converts when `_wc_label != currency.upper()` and returns WITHOUT touching source_method. Compare JSON-LD :12876, OG :12701, microdata :13503-13504 and RSC :13603, each of which sets `result["source_method"] = "converted_usd"` in the same position. Executed: a 195.00 EUR Woo span on a BHD request returns {'amount': 79.95, 'original_currency': 'EUR', 'currency': 'BHD', 'source_method': 'page_scrape'}; `_is_genuine_bh_candidate` -> True, `price_cache_ttl` -> 604800 (7 days), `is_price_showable` -> True.
findings.failure_scenario: Any WooCommerce PDP in a non-target currency (the microdata docstring at :13491 already names five such cached hosts — klinq.com, ardalzaafaranshop.com, bawwaba.om, armaf.ae, spinneyslebanon.com). The converted figure (a) is cached 7 days instead of 24h, (b) is counted by the genuine-BH-share KPI the whole 'faithful results' programme is measured on, (c) passes `_confirmed()` in `fan_out_price_lookup` (:15427 filters on `_is_genuine_bh_candidate`) so it ENDS the race and cancels a still-pending genuine BH scraper — the exact regression `_confirmed`'s own docstring (:15422-15426) says it exists to prevent, and (d) is never shown with the 'indicative/reference' honesty caption converted prices are supposed to carry.
findings.fix_sketch: Inside the `if _wc_label != currency.upper():` block at :13119, after the strict-label pend check, add `result["source_method"] = "converted_usd"` — the identical line the four sibling branches already carry. Gate on `jsonld_first_enabled()` if flag-OFF byte-identity is required, matching the microdata branch's `if _first:` at :13503.

findings.title: WooCommerce branch parses the amount under the ASK currency but labels it from PAGE evidence — the minor-unit divisor and the stamped currency come from different currencies
findings.claim: `detected_currency` (used for the minor-unit tie-break) falls back to the EXPECTED currency while `_wc_label` (used for the label and the conversion) falls back to `_page_currency_evidence`, so a span with no readable symbol child is parsed as BHD (minor unit 3) and then converted as EUR/USD/whatever the page metas say.
findings.evidence: price_service.py:13075 `detected_currency = (_raw_wc_symbol or currency).strip().upper()` — `currency` is the ASK. :13083-13086 `_wc_label = _currency_label_for(_raw_wc_symbol, currency, soup)` — rung 2 consults `_page_currency_evidence(soup)`. :13095-13097 parses with `detected_currency`. The comment at :13081 asserts 'the two must not disagree' but that only holds for rung 1. Executed: a Woo span `<bdi>1.234</bdi>` with no currencySymbol child on a page whose only currency signal is `og:price:currency=EUR` returns {'amount': 0.51, 'original_currency': 'EUR', 'currency': 'BHD', 'source_method': 'page_scrape'}; `parse_price_string('1.234','BHD',display_text=True)` = 1.234 vs `parse_price_string('1.234','EUR',display_text=True)` = 1234.0.
findings.failure_scenario: A EUR/GBP/USD WooCommerce PDP writing a dot-grouped thousands price (de-DE '1.234', the shape `parse_money` rule 5 hands to the currency) is read as 1.234 instead of 1234.0 and then converted EUR->BHD: EUR 1,234 ships as 0.51 BHD — a ~2,400x UNDER-price that passes the only downstream magnitude guard (`amount > 0`) and wins every cheapest-price comparison. Combined with finding 01 it also ships labelled `page_scrape`, i.e. as a genuine Bahrain shelf price, cached 7 days.
findings.fix_sketch: Resolve the label FIRST and parse with it: compute `_wc_label` before the parse and pass `_wc_label` (not `detected_currency`) into `parse_price_string` when `jsonld_first_enabled()`. Keep `detected_currency` only for the flag-OFF path so the rollback stays byte-identical. Add a pin asserting the parse currency and the stamped currency are the same token.

findings.title: Serper-shopping tier has no strict-currency guard: a GCC display token is invisible to `detect_currency`, so the raw foreign amount is stamped with the target currency and labelled `local_bhd` (genuine)
findings.claim: `detect_currency` reads only the 4-glyph `CURRENCY_SYMBOLS` and 11-code `CURRENCY_CODES` tables and never consults `GCC_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS`/`_normalize_currency_code`, so every GCC display token returns None; `extract_price_from_shopping` then performs no conversion, stamps `currency: <target>` and `source_method: local_bhd`.
findings.evidence: price_service.py:3371-3382 (`detect_currency` iterates CURRENCY_SYMBOLS at :545 and CURRENCY_CODES at :546-550 only). price_service.py:9339-9355 (`detected_cur = detect_currency(price_str)`; conversion and the `item_converted` flag BOTH gate on a truthy `detected_cur`); :9432 stamps `"currency": currency`; :9438 stamps `local_bhd` when `item_converted` is False. Executed: `detect_currency` returns None for 'د.إ 350.00', 'SR 1,299', 'KD 45.500', 'ر.ق 199', 'QR 199' while `_normalize_currency_code` resolves each to AED/SAR/KWD/QAR/QAR. A Noon item priced 'د.إ 1,399.00' returns {'amount': 1399.0, 'currency': 'BHD', 'source_method': 'local_bhd'}; `_is_genuine_bh_candidate` True, `is_price_showable` True, `price_cache_ttl` 604800.
findings.failure_scenario: AED 1,399 ships as 1399 BHD (truth 143.3 BHD at the pinned 0.1024 rate) — a 9.8x over-price labelled as a GENUINE Bahrain shelf price, showable, counted in the genuine-share KPI and cached 7 days. This is BLOCKER-4's exact failure mode (price_service.py:555-560 describes it verbatim) surviving on the one tier the fix never covered: `extract_price_from_shopping` never calls `_convert_gpt_price_currency` and never reads `strict_currency_label_enabled()`. Reachability: the `local_bhd` label needs the gl=<country> shopping primary to return items, i.e. `SERPER_SHOPPING_PRIMARY_COUNTRIES` set — which CLAUDE.md explicitly invites ('set e.g. bh,ae to buy it again if a real feed appears'). On today's default us_fallback leg the same UN-CONVERTED amount still ships, labelled `converted_usd`.
findings.fix_sketch: Make `detect_currency` delegate to `_normalize_currency_code` after its own tables miss (one line: `return _normalize_currency_code(price_str) or None` as the tail), and add the strict-label pend to `extract_price_from_shopping`: when `detected_cur` is None on a non-target-currency-looking string, or when `_normalize_currency_code(detected_cur)` is None, skip the candidate instead of stamping the target currency. Also fix the `'$' in 'R$'` collision (BRL 799 currently converts as USD to 300.42 BHD, verified).

findings.title: The same Serper shopping price string is parsed two different ways inside one request — a 1000x divergence feeds the pair-fairness re-selection pool
findings.claim: `_seed_shortcircuit_candidates` calls `parse_price_string(price_str)` with neither the detected currency nor `display_text=True`, while `extract_price_from_shopping` parses the identical string with both — producing different amounts for the same listing in the same request.
findings.evidence: structured_comparison_service.py:7245 `amount = parse_price_string(price_str)` vs price_service.py:9340 `amount = parse_price_string(price_str, detected_cur, display_text=True)`. Executed on this tree: 'BHD 12,500' -> main 12.5 / stash 12500.0 (1000x); 'KWD 1,250' -> 1.25 / 1250.0 (1000x); 'BHD 22,902' -> 22.902 / 22902.0; '2.019 TL' -> 2019.0 / 2.019 (0.001x). The stash also ignores `shopping_region`, so a gl=us item is labelled `local_bhd` here (scs:7286) where the main path labels it `converted_usd` (price_service.py:9438).
findings.failure_scenario: Seeded candidates are appended to `self._price_candidates[full_name]` (scs:7303) and consumed by `reselect_to_target_value` / `reselect_to_target_size` inside `reconcile_pair_fairness`. The only gate is `is_price_showable(full_name, price)` (scs:7292) WITHOUT `enforce_correctness`, and none of its guards is an upper-magnitude check for fragrances (`is_implausible_low_fragrance_price` catches LOW only). So a Bahraini 12.500 BHD listing can re-enter the pool as 12500.0 BHD and be re-selected as the served price when the pair needs a different size basis.
findings.fix_sketch: Thread the same arguments: `detected = detect_currency(price_str)` already exists two lines below at scs:7248 — hoist it above the parse and call `parse_price_string(price_str, detected, display_text=True)`. Also pass `shopping_region` into `_seed_shortcircuit_candidates` and reuse the `region_is_us_fallback` rule so the two labels agree. Best fix: have the stash reuse `extract_price_from_shopping`'s per-item normalisation rather than re-implementing it.

findings.title: `ENABLE_RSC_FLIGHT_PRICE` is a dead rung: its entire measured cohort (3/3 cached TRY pages) pends under the shipped default `ENABLE_STRICT_CURRENCY_LABEL=true`
findings.claim: The RSC flight rung converts through `_convert_gpt_price_currency`, which resolves currencies only against the 13-entry `FALLBACK_RATES`; TRY is absent, so strict mode returns False and the rung returns None for every sephora.com.tr page it was built and measured on.
findings.evidence: price_service.py:13596-13603 (`if cur.upper() != currency.upper(): _ok = _convert_gpt_price_currency(...); if strict_currency_label_enabled() and not _ok: return None`). `_convert_gpt_price_currency`:768-777 returns False when `_normalize_currency_code` is None. `_normalize_currency_code`:622-631 checks only `FALLBACK_RATES` (exchange_rate_service.py:18-32 — USD EUR GBP SGD JPY CNY INR SAR AED KWD QAR OMR BHD) then `GCC_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS`. Executed: `_extract_rsc_flight_price(<flight html with "price":5050,"currency":"TRY">, 'BHD', ...)` returns None; `_normalize_currency_code('TRY')` returns None; the docstring at :13526-13527 names exactly those three TRY rows as the rung's whole evidence base.
findings.failure_scenario: Step (1) of the ACTIVATION-ORDER runbook flips `ENABLE_RSC_FLIGHT_PRICE` alongside six other flags and measures the canary. The rung contributes zero on its own corpus, so the canary reads as 'no regression, no gain' and the flag is either left on as inert code or judged a failed unit — while the actual blocker (a 13-currency rate table) is never named. The same ceiling silently pends every capture in TRY/PLN/SEK/DKK/CAD/EGP/JOD/CHF — currencies `iso_currency_label`'s own docstring (:11239) says appear in the corpora.
findings.fix_sketch: Either (a) widen `FALLBACK_RATES` to cover the corpus currencies before flipping the flag, or (b) wire `_convert_to_bhd`/`_normalize_currency_code` to the live rate table `exchange_rate_service._fetch_rates()` already knows how to fetch (see finding 06), or (c) record in the runbook that the RSC rung is inert until a TRY rate exists, so step (1)'s canary is not read as evidence about it.

findings.title: `exchange_rate_service.get_rate()` has ZERO production callers — every conversion runs on a 13-currency table hardcoded 'as of 2026-05'
findings.claim: The live-rate path (Frankfurter fetch, 24h Redis cache, cross-rate lookup, unknown->1.0 fallback) is never invoked by the deployed backend; all eleven conversion sites import `FALLBACK_RATES` directly.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn get_rate --include=*.py .` in this tree returns exactly one definition (exchange_rate_service.py:56) and 20 references, ALL inside tests/test_exchange_rate_service.py. The eleven production conversion sites all read the dict: price_service.py:622, :707, :14245; algolia_service.py:892; magento_graphql_service.py:1166; occ_service.py:48; rest_json_service.py:185; shopify_pdp_service.py:1022; unbxd_service.py:262; woocommerce_service.py:252; salla_service.py:71 (a hand-copied mirror set).
findings.failure_scenario: Two costs. (1) The floating rates — EUR 0.41, GBP 0.475, SGD 0.282, JPY, CNY, INR — are frozen at their 2026-05 values and cannot drift-correct; every `converted_usd` price in those currencies carries that error permanently. (2) `_fallback_rate` (:127-141) returns **1.0** for an unknown currency with only a warning — the precise implicit-1.0 stamp the whole BLOCKER-4 wave exists to eliminate — sitting live in a function that will be correct-looking the day someone wires `get_rate` in. CLAUDE.md's Key-services block states 'Daily rates from frankfurter.app, Redis-cached 24h ... get_rate(from, to="BHD")', so the documented status is WRONG.
findings.fix_sketch: Decide one way: either delete `get_rate`/`_fetch_rates`/`_lookup_rate`/`_fallback_rate` and their tests and correct CLAUDE.md, or make `_convert_to_bhd` async-or-cached over the live table and delete `_fallback_rate`'s 1.0 branch in favour of returning None. Do not leave a 1.0-returning rate function reachable by name.

findings.title: Eight direct-fetch adapters hard-code `"currency": "BHD"` and ignore their own `currency` parameter — any non-Bahrain GCC region gets BHD-denominated prices with no cross-currency check anywhere downstream
findings.claim: The BH/GCC adapter tier converts everything to BHD and stamps the literal 'BHD' regardless of the request's region currency, and neither `is_price_showable` nor `response_builder` compares a price's currency against the requested one.
findings.evidence: Hardcoded stamps: salla_service.py:275 and :295 (signature at :181 takes `currency: str = "BHD"` and never reads it), occ_service.py:227 (signature :255), woocommerce_service.py:266 (signature :299), rest_json_service.py:175 and :190 (signature :496), unbxd_service.py:66 and :275, algolia_service.py:97/:104/:807/:905, magento_graphql_service.py:1177, noon_service.py:444. `region` is a public request parameter accepting all six GCC regions (text_routes.py:251, :386, :641, defaulting to 'bahrain'), and `_get_price` derives `currency = region_info["currency"]` (structured_comparison_service.py:5184) from `GCC_REGIONS` (extraction_service.py:55+). `grep -n currency app/services/response_builder.py` returns only :1228/:1242/:1257 — none of them a target-vs-actual comparison; `is_price_showable` (price_service.py:1628) never inspects `price["currency"]`.
findings.failure_scenario: A `region=saudi_arabia` compare (currency SAR): product A resolves through a BH adapter and returns 25.0 stamped 'BHD'; product B resolves through the Serper/GPT tier and returns 250.0 stamped 'SAR'. Scoring, the value badges, the cheapest-price comparison and the frontend all read `product.price.amount` as a bare number (documented at price_service.py:743-746), so product A wins a 10x-wrong comparison and the card renders 'BHD 25.0' to a Saudi user. Nothing in the pipeline can detect it, because the currency FIELD is never checked against the region.
findings.fix_sketch: Short term: add one guard at the response chokepoint — `is_price_showable` (or `build_comparison_response`) pends any price whose `currency` differs from the request's region currency, and log it. Medium term: have each adapter honour its `currency` parameter (they already compute a BHD amount; convert BHD->target via `_convert_to_bhd(1.0, target)` and stamp `target`), or make the registry region-aware so BH-tier sources are not consulted for a non-BH region.

findings.title: A well-formed JSON-LD PDP in any non-target, non-USD currency returns NO price — the extractor hard-continues and only retries USD, pushing every GCC cross-border page onto the defect-carrying fallback branches
findings.claim: `extract_jsonld_price` drops every Offer whose `priceCurrency` is not string-equal to `expected_currency`, and `extract_price_from_html` retries only with 'USD' — so an AED/SAR/QAR/OMR/KWD JSON-LD page is invisible to the single most reliable rung.
findings.evidence: price_service.py:10601-10602 `if str(currency).upper() != expected_currency.upper(): continue`. price_service.py:10824-10830 — the only retry is `extract_jsonld_price(html, brand, "USD", ...)`. The consequence is stated in-code at :12528-12529 ('extract_jsonld_price hard-continues on a currency mismatch and only retries "USD", so a SAR/AED/KWD/QAR/OMR page always lands HERE'). Executed on a synthetic AED Product+Offer PDP: `extract_jsonld_price(..., 'BHD')` -> None, `... 'USD'` -> None, `... 'AED'` -> the correct 499.0; `extract_price_from_html(..., 'BHD')` -> None for the whole page.
findings.failure_scenario: CLAUDE.md's own global validation says 353 of 360 JSON-LD prices are machine-normalised while OG is 11% deviant and 'the real answer is architectural: take the price from JSON-LD, always'. This gate throws that away for exactly the Gulf cross-border storefronts the product targets, and routes them to the OG / microdata / WooCommerce branches — which is where findings 01 and 02 live. The page either pends (no other structured shape) or is priced by the branch with the weakest currency handling.
findings.fix_sketch: Accept a foreign-currency Offer as a candidate carrying its OWN `priceCurrency`, then run it through the same `_convert_gpt_price_currency` + strict-label + `converted_usd` relabel the sibling branches use — i.e. replace the hard-continue with the cascade's standard convert-or-pend. Gate it on its own flag with a corpus before/after, since it changes which branch wins on every Gulf cross-border page.

findings.title: An EMPTY env value silently DISABLES every default-ON correctness flag, and only those — the polarity footgun fires in exactly the unsafe direction
findings.claim: Default-ON readers use `os.getenv(NAME, "true") not in ("false","0","no","off","")`, so a variable that exists but is blank evaluates to OFF; default-OFF readers use `in ("true","1","yes","on")`, where blank is inert.
findings.evidence: Default-ON, blank == OFF: `strict_currency_label_enabled` :677, `money_parser_v2_enabled` :3300, `exact_gate_enabled` :4000-4005, `sale_price_first_enabled` :4007+, `og_branch_fixes_enabled` :4089+, `hostile_numeric_guard_enabled` :4210+, `wide_candidate_enabled` :4135+, `jsonld_shape_ladder_enabled` :10024, `jsonld_first_enabled` :11146+, `_budget_fragrance_floor_enabled` :4303, `_fairness_ignore_estimate_enabled` :4403, `adapter_query_ladder_enabled` :6246+, `adapter_selection_primary_enabled` :6256+. Default-OFF, blank == OFF (safe): `not_a_pdp_filter_enabled` :11909, `visible_text_currency_enabled` :11270, `wall_anchor_enabled` :11767, `rsc_flight_price_enabled`, `extractor_fixes_2608_enabled`, `variant_min_guard_enabled`.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator adds `ENABLE_STRICT_CURRENCY_LABEL` to Railway during the activation runbook and saves it with an empty value (or a `.env` line `ENABLE_EXACT_PRICE_GATE=`). The flag reads OFF and the pipeline silently reverts to the pre-fix behaviour: the 32,000-BHD perfume stamp (strict label), the '320,00' -> 32000 100x (money parser), cheapest-pick selection plus a fully-open cache-write gate plus internal `_cached`/`guard_rejected` keys leaking into the public price object (exact gate, price_service.py:8794 and :8869). Nothing logs the transition.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a shared `_flag(name, default: bool)` helper that treats an empty/whitespace value as ABSENT (i.e. use the default) and only an explicit off-token as OFF, then route all 53 readers through it. Log one INFO line per flag at first read naming the effective value, mirroring the `[BUDGET] serper spend gate ENGAGED/INERT` pattern.

findings.title: 21 of the 53 `ENABLE_*` flags the deployed backend reads are absent from CLAUDE.md — including 10 default-ON price-correctness flags whose rollback re-arms documented P0s
findings.claim: The Feature-Flags block and the ACTIVATION-ORDER runbook do not name `ENABLE_STRICT_CURRENCY_LABEL`, `ENABLE_MONEY_PARSER_V2`, `ENABLE_JSONLD_SHAPE_LADDER`, `ENABLE_SALE_PRICE_FIRST`, `ENABLE_OG_BRANCH_FIXES`, `ENABLE_HOSTILE_NUMERIC_GUARD`, `ENABLE_WIDE_CANDIDATE`, `ENABLE_BUDGET_FRAGRANCE_FLOOR`, `ENABLE_ADAPTER_QUERY_LADDER`, `ENABLE_ADAPTER_SELECTION_PRIMARY` (all default ON) or 11 further flags.
findings.evidence: Enumerated every `os.getenv("ENABLE_*")` under app/services + app/utils (53 distinct names) and grepped each against CLAUDE.md. Absent: ADAPTER_QUERY_LADDER, ADAPTER_SELECTION_PRIMARY, ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD, BRIGHTDATA_BUDGET_GATE, BUDGET_FRAGRANCE_FLOOR, FRAGRANCE_SIZE_RECONCILE_FIX, GENUINE_PRICE_PRIORITY, HOSTILE_NUMERIC_GUARD, JSONLD_SHAPE_LADDER, MONEY_PARSER_V2, OG_BRANCH_FIXES, ORGANIC_PDP_HARVEST, PARK_LISTING_URL_TIER1, PRICE_TITLE_PERSIST, SALE_PRICE_FIRST, SERPER_FAIL_FAST, STRICT_CURRENCY_LABEL, VARIANT_DESCRIPTOR_AXES, VARIANT_LLM_HINT, VARIANT_MIN_PRICE_GUARD, WIDE_CANDIDATE. CLAUDE.md's wave-3 block claims '11 flags total'.
findings.failure_scenario: A flag nobody knows exists is a flag nobody canaries, nobody rolls back deliberately, and nobody checks after an incident. Concretely: `ENABLE_HOSTILE_NUMERIC_GUARD=false` does not degrade — price_service.py:10425-10426 RE-RAISES the ValueError, so a JSON-LD block with a >4300-digit numeric literal crashes `extract_price_from_html` into the two scraper call sites that do not wrap it. `ENABLE_MONEY_PARSER_V2=false` restores a measured 100x. `ENABLE_STRICT_CURRENCY_LABEL=false` restores the 32,000-BHD stamp. None of the three is discoverable from the operator-facing docs.
findings.fix_sketch: Generate the flag inventory rather than hand-maintaining it: a small script that greps `os.getenv("ENABLE_` across app/ and emits name + default + defining function + one-line effect, run in CI and diffed against a committed table. Add the 10 default-ON price flags to the runbook with an explicit 'rollback re-arms <named P0>' note.

findings.title: The NOT-A-PDP verdict is computed and then bypassed by all three side-door channels flipped in the same activation step
findings.claim: `fetch_page_price` consults `CAPTURE_NOT_A_PDP` only AFTER the Magento-GQL, Salla-slug and UCP-JSON fallbacks have run, so a page the filter classified as an offsite redirect, a category page or a branded error shell still issues up to three network calls, and any price they return is served with no `capture_outcome`.
findings.evidence: price_service.py:13792-13826 — `_try_magento_gql_url_fallback` (:13795), `_try_salla_slug_resolve` (:13804), `_try_ucp_json_price` (:13813), and only then `if _outcomes is not None and CAPTURE_NOT_A_PDP in _outcomes: return None` (:13824). The comment at :13819-13823 justifies the ordering for B5 (Salla) alone. `extract_price_from_html` returns None at :12805 before `_finish`, so `price["capture_outcome"]` is never stamped on whatever the side doors produce. The ACTIVATION-ORDER runbook puts `ENABLE_NOT_A_PDP_FILTER`, `ENABLE_MAGENTO_GQL_ADAPTER`, `ENABLE_SALLA_SLUG_RESOLVE` and `ENABLE_UCP_JSON_PRICE` in the SAME step (1).
findings.failure_scenario: The E1 census's `NOT_A_PDP_REDIRECT_OFFSITE` rows (thebay.com -> canadiantire.ca, seifonline.com -> hugedomains.com) and `NOT_A_PDP_CATEGORY_PAGE` rows still pay a Magento GraphQL POST + a Salla search API call + a `/products/{handle}.json` GET each, against a URL that was never a product page — so the very cost the filter exists to remove is only removed for the HTML rung. Worse, a UCP or Magento hit on such a URL is returned as a normal price with no outcome stamp, so the M9 measurement ('never priced, never counted as render candidates', :11880-11881) is not what the code does when the four flags are on together.
findings.fix_sketch: Move the `CAPTURE_NOT_A_PDP` check directly after `extract_price_from_html` returns None, keeping ONLY the Salla-slug side door below it (that one is documented as a deliberate homepage-collapse recovery and can be re-gated on `_na_reason == NOT_A_PDP_REDIRECT_HOMEPAGE`). Stamp `capture_outcome` on any side-door price so the outcome census stays total.

findings.title: `_convert_gpt_price_currency` and the Tier-2 label branch crash on `original_currency: null`
findings.claim: `price.get("original_currency", "").upper()` raises AttributeError when the key is present with value None — an in-distribution LLM output, since the price prompt's own JSON schema shows sibling fields as `null`.
findings.evidence: price_service.py:760 and the identical expression at structured_comparison_service.py:6795. The prompt schema at extraction_service.py:833-842 renders `"retailer": null, "url": null` next to `"original_currency": "USD"`, and `sanitize_gpt_price` (price_service.py:9159-9168) normalises only `retailer` and `url`. The call at structured_comparison_service.py:6754 is unguarded. Executed: `_convert_gpt_price_currency({'amount':699.0,'original_currency':None,'currency':'BHD'}, 'BHD')` -> AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'upper'.
findings.failure_scenario: The Tier-2 GPT-organic extract returns `"original_currency": null` for a snippet with no currency symbol; `_get_price` raises out of the tier cascade instead of degrading to Tier 3, so the product's price is lost for that request (and, because the raise happens before any cache write, re-lost on every retry).
findings.fix_sketch: One line at each site: `original = str(price.get("original_currency") or "").upper()`. Add the same coercion to `sanitize_gpt_price` so every LLM-sourced price dict is normalised once at the boundary, matching the `_jsonld_str` boundary-coercion pattern the JSON-LD path already uses.

findings.title: `quality_ranker` is unreferenced, and the `confirmed_multi_source` method it emits would be un-showable if it were ever wired in
findings.claim: `select_best_price` has no caller in app/ or scripts/, and its output `source_method: "confirmed_multi_source"` is in neither `_GENUINE_BH_SOURCE_METHODS` nor `_showable_source_methods()`, so every price it produced would pend at the display chokepoint.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'quality_ranker|select_best_price' app/ scripts/` returns only the definition plus two comments (structured_comparison_service.py:1293-1296 says it maintains a private mirror of `PRICE_SOURCE_RANK` to avoid importing the module, and price_service.py:13475 names it as a consumer that does not exist). `_showable_source_methods()` = `_GENUINE_BH_SOURCE_METHODS | {"converted_usd"}` (price_service.py:1591); `_GENUINE_BH_SOURCE_METHODS` (:15445-15467) does not contain `confirmed_multi_source`, nor `serper_shopping` or `gpt_training_estimate`, two more entries of `PRICE_SOURCE_RANK`. cache_service.py:234 meanwhile documents `confirmed_multi_source` as a REAL price for the coverage gauge — so the two ends already disagree about a string nothing produces.
findings.failure_scenario: Cost is measurable but latent: 45 lines plus a duplicated rank table that must be kept in sync by hand (scs:1293), and a booby trap — wiring the ranker in (the obvious 'use the scatter-gather winner' change) would make every multi-source-confirmed price invisible at the chokepoint and 24h-TTL'd, with no test covering the combination.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete `app/services/quality_ranker.py` and its rank table, or, if it is intended future work, add `confirmed_multi_source` to `_GENUINE_BH_SOURCE_METHODS` and a test pinning `PRICE_SOURCE_RANK`'s method names as a subset of `_showable_source_methods() | {"gpt_training_estimate"}`.
